findings.desc: CHK-002 adversarial:0 was authored from a false premise and one of its two clauses is unsatisfiable on this branch. The intent text reads 'the local d3 hard-failure branch in scripts/build-web.mjs survives the port AND dossier.js is concatenated after app.js, not before'. The d3 hard-failure change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the MAIN checkout; it is not committed on story/B-9f2c and it is not upstream either. Verified two ways: grep -c 'd3 is missing' packages/graph/scripts/build-web.mjs returns 0 on this branch, and the CHK-002 implementer independently reported build-web.mjs is now byte-identical to upstream. So no work on this branch can either satisfy or violate that clause. The load-order clause is the real risk and IS proven: build-web.mjs concatenates app.js at line 33, playback.js at 36 and dossier.js at 40, and the recorded evidence for this intent pins that ordering with a negative control. No evidence was fabricated for the d3 clause; the implementer recorded its voiding in the evidence note. Deliberately NOT fixed by rewriting the intent: verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN by design, and checklist_update correctly refused the edit. Rewriting a frozen intent mid-DEV to match what was actually built is exactly the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Filing this instead so the mismatch is auditable rather than silently reworded.
findings.resolvedReason: Accepted as a documented, non-blocking record rather than fixed, because the only available fix is prohibited by design. The defect is in the WORDING of a frozen PLAN artifact, not in shipped behavior: CHK-002:adversarial:0 bundles two clauses, and the d3 hard-failure clause is unsatisfiable on this branch. Independently re-verified three ways by the test-coverage reviewer (B-9f2c:RP-004), which confirmed the d3 branch exists only as an uncommitted diff in the unrelated main checkout, is absent from git log and grep on story/B-9f2c, and is absent from upstream proof-or-stop-graph as well. The load-order clause, which is the real risk that intent exists to guard, IS genuinely evidenced: RP-004 reconstructed the regression itself, moving dossier.js ahead of app.js in build-web.mjs, and confirmed the probe fails closed with DOSSIER_LOAD_ORDER_FAIL exit 1. No evidence was fabricated for the void clause. Rewriting the intent to match what was built was attempted and correctly REFUSED by checklist_update, since verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN; doing so would be exactly the self-absolution that freeze exists to prevent. Per CLAUDE.md defect triage, this is non-blocking (low severity, no gate distortion, no acceptance impact: AB-001 does not bind CHK-002:adversarial:0) and unclaimed by any checklist item, so it is recorded and deferred with full evidence rather than fixed by scope creep. RP-004 explicitly reviewed this handling and agreed with it. Follow-up for a future story, if desired: split multi-clause verificationIntent entries into one clause each at authoring time, so a single void clause cannot strand an otherwise-satisfied intent.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md:111-115 (section 'Test-surface placement') states 'Two test lists in this repository are separately maintained, and neither is a subset of the other: validate.commands in the project config, and test:serial-reference in the root package.json.' This is incomplete: packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY (lines 116-159) is a THIRD fail-closed membership authority -- entriesFromSerialReference (full-suite-runner.ts:216-227) throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the whole suite (called at line 590 of main(), before any test entry is scheduled) if a test:serial-reference member has no RESOURCE_POLICY entry. This story's own CHK-005 checklist context explicitly modeled its plan on this doc's 'TWO separate test-surface lists' framing and, as a direct consequence, registered the new graph-story-flag-smoke task in validate.commands and test:serial-reference but not in RESOURCE_POLICY -- causing npm test to abort in 858ms with exactly the unknownPolicy error the code comments describe, which blocked done_required_validate and forced a TEST->DEV->REVIEW bounce (fixed in commit f4e9acdd21). The code's own comments at full-suite-runner.ts:145-146 and :151-153 record that this identical trap was already hit twice before by other stories (B-49ed, B-cdf6), meaning the canonical decision doc has been silently incomplete across at least three incidents. A future implementer who reads only this doc (as CHK-005 did) will reproduce the same suite-aborting failure. Severity high: this is the specific reproducible-bug-inducing doc gap the review task explicitly asked to check for, and the doc is the canonical decision reference cited by this story's own checklist relatedDocs.
